population.span: Patients were randomized if they were admitted to an ICU and needed at least 1 fluid expansion (at the discretion of the attending physician), were not expected to be discharged the next day after enrollment, and met at least 1 of the following criteria for acute kidney injury:

endpoint.span: Outcomes Primary Outcome The primary outcome was 90-day survival.

estimate.span: Within 90 days, 1381 of 5230 patients (26.4%) assigned to a balanced solution died vs 1439 of 5290 patients (27.2%) assigned to saline solution (adjusted HR, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.90-1.05]; P = .47).

ci.span: Within 90 days, 1381 of 5230 patients (26.4%) assigned to a balanced solution died vs 1439 of 5290 patients (27.2%) assigned to saline solution (adjusted HR, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.90-1.05]; P = .47).

analysis_set.span: 486 patients subsequently refused to provide consent and 46 were duplicate patients [the first enrollment for those patients was kept in the analysis]), leaving 10 520 patients for the analysis (5230 patients randomized to a balanced solution and 5290 randomized to saline solution; Figure 1 ).

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive either a balanced solution (n = 5522) or 0.9% saline solution (n = 5530) for all intravenous fluids.

follow_up.span: A follow-up contact was performed (centrally at the HCor Research Institute) by telephone at 90 days after enrollment to assess vital status and need for kidney replacement therapy after discharge.

served_mismatch: The served HR and confidence interval match the reported adjusted HR for 90-day mortality. However, the requested estimand is RR; this HR and its interval cannot be treated as an RR. The served intention-to-treat label also requires qualification: the source explicitly excludes patients after randomization and reports an analysis of 10 520 patients rather than all 11 052 randomized patients.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The entry population comprised ICU patients requiring fluid expansion with an acute kidney injury risk factor; the registry confirms eligibility was restricted to adults. The analysis-set limitation is separate from entry eligibility.
entry_population_matches_question.span: ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 18 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL

notes: Full-text spans were preferred; the registry span supplies the explicit adult age restriction. The numeric HR candidate is retained because it matches the source endpoint and timepoint. Counts are reported as printed; no RR or RR confidence interval was inferred. The full text identifies the balanced solution as Plasma-Lyte 148 and requests trial fluids for fluid challenges, maintenance fluids, and drug infusions greater than 100 mL during the ICU stay up to 90 days. The source describes censoring and imputation for missing primary-outcome data.
